name: Water filters
anchor: EU food-contact framework Regulation 1935/2004 with Regulation (EU) 10/2011 Annex II specific migration limits as the only element-migration instrument in the register; polymer-surface rows anchor it directly or by disclosed read-across, and metal, alloy, ceramic-glaze, vitreous-enamel and glass rows are controls because their dedicated release regimes are not yet ingested.
cross_reference: Cross-links to Category 8 (drinking water and beverages) for the water-basis parametric values and to the treatment-device sub-platform; never pooled with the alloy-leach or glaze-leach bands of this category.
native_basis: element release from the treatment device into the treated water (µg/L, reported as µg/kg)
native_basis_label: NET ELEMENT RELEASE FROM THE TREATMENT DEVICE INTO THE TREATED WATER, µg/L reported as µg/kg, determined as device effluent minus a matched influent blank so that any contribution BY the device is resolved separately from what the device removes. This is a device-release basis on the water leaving the device; the sovereign drinking-water parametric values are a WATER basis on the supply as delivered and are disclosed as companions, never republished as the device's release ceiling.
scope_note: The assembled point-of-use treatment device. This row must be scoped honestly in both directions, because a filter is an INTERVENTION WHOSE PURPOSE IS TO REMOVE METALS: the certification question is not only whether treated water meets a limit, which the influent may already have done, but whether the device itself CONTRIBUTES any element to the water it treats, and separately whether it delivers the reduction it claims across its rated life. Both are mandatory determinations here. No credible sovereign sets an element release ceiling for a treatment device, so the row is a control; the EU Directive 2020/2184 route is an Art. 11 hygiene-and-positive-list regime rather than element release values, the US route is the SDWA lead-free content definition plus NSF/ANSI 61 conformity, and neither is in the register. Sovereign drinking-water parametric values are disclosed as WATER-basis companions on the treated water and are never republished as the device's release ceiling. A device must never be credited for the influent's cleanliness, and reduction performance must never be inferred from a low effluent result on clean influent.
basis_guard: element release from the treatment device into the treated water
basis_guard_note: Only an instrument expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant may anchor a cell on this row. The guard exists to reject the three foreign bases that surround this category and would otherwise look plausible: the FOOD basis (canned-food tin maximum levels, which limit the contents and not the article), the MATERIAL-CONTENT basis (CPSIA total lead in substrate, EU REACH Annex XVII cadmium percent-by-weight restrictions, RoHS homogeneous-material limits, Japan Notice 370 and Korea MFDS percent-by-weight lead in food-contact metals), and the ARTICLE-EXTRACTION basis of the toy regime (EU 2009/48 Annex II Part III and ASTM F963 soluble limits, which are element migration from scraped-off or coated TOY material into 0.07 M hydrochloric acid, expressed per kg of MATERIAL, not per kg of food). Any of those would fail this guard and resolve to a gap rather than publish in the wrong basis. On this control row the guard is declaratory as well as operative: it records the only basis in which a future ingested instrument would be allowed to supply this row's numbers, so that a content limit, a food limit, a water limit or a plastics specific migration limit cannot later be dropped in as this row's release ceiling. The plastics clause is deliberately absent from this guard: a Reg (EU) 10/2011 value named here would fail the guard and resolve to a gap.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form expressed as specific element migration into food or a food simulant; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign value in the same basis where the food-contact material family is expressly excluded from or not reached by that instrument; a substantiated not-material determination; or a control. No cell is occurrence-derived, and no cell borrows a value across a basis.

Pb.rationale: A drinking-water treatment device is an intervention whose purpose is to REMOVE metals, so the certification question is not whether the effluent meets a food limit but whether the device itself contributes any element to the water it treats. No credible sovereign sets a release ceiling for a treatment device or its media: the EU regulates materials in contact with water intended for human consumption through the Art. 11 hygiene-requirement and positive-list route of Directive (EU) 2020/2184 rather than through element release values, the US route is the SDWA lead-free content definition plus NSF/ANSI 61 conformity, and neither is a sovereign element release ceiling in this register. Regulation (EU) 10/2011 does not reach the media at all: Art. 2(2)(a) expressly excludes ion exchange resins from its scope. The cell is therefore a control with mandatory net-contribution testing against a matched influent blank, and the sovereign drinking-water parametric value is disclosed as a companion obligation in the WATER basis, never republished as a device release ceiling. Lead is the element a filter is most often bought to remove, and it is simultaneously a possible device contribution from leaded brass fittings, bronze bodies and soldered joints in the wetted path. Both directions are tested: net contribution against a matched influent blank, and removal performance against the challenge influent. The sovereign drinking-water parametric value disclosed as this cell's companion is a limit on the WATER as delivered; it is not the device's release ceiling and is not published as one. The two mandatory determinations on this row are net device contribution against a matched influent blank and reduction performance at end of rated life; either one alone misrepresents the device.
Pb.reference_method: Device-effluent extraction testing on the conditioned device: influent of defined composition passed through the device at rated flow, effluent sampled at first draw, after the manufacturer's conditioning volume, and at rated capacity, with ICP-MS determination of each element in the effluent and comparison against the matched influent blank so that any net contribution by the device is resolved separately from what the device removes.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food chains and is not a constituent of, nor a contribution from, a filter housing, a filter medium or a wetted metal fitting. No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for a drinking-water treatment device or for drinking water itself, in any basis. Total mercury remains a mandatory control on this row for both device contribution and reduction performance; methylmercury is not material and never substitutes for it.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury determination in device effluent per the tHg control; no methylmercury reflex is defined for a treatment device, and biofilm-bearing spent media are handled by the end-of-life change-out rule rather than by a methylmercury ceiling.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury requirement for a drinking-water treatment device, its media, or water intended for human consumption. Directive (EU) 2020/2184 Annex I and the US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations both state mercury as the total element.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (Reg (EU) 1935/2004 framework + Annex I material families; Reg (EU) 10/2011 Annex II element list, as amended by 2016/1416 and 2020/1245); UK (retained Reg 10/2011); US (FDA food-contact substances, 21 CFR 174-190: no element migration ceiling for these elements); Codex (no food-contact-material standard); AU-NZ (FSANZ Food Standards Code 1.4.3 and 3.2.2: no element migration ceiling); Canada (Food and Drugs Act s.4 / letter-of-no-objection route, no numeric element migration ceiling); Hong Kong (Cap 132 subsidiary legislation: food limits only).
